record.paper_title: 1-Bend 3-D Orthogonal Box-Drawings: Two Open Problems Solved
record.original_question: Does every graph admit a three-dimensional orthogonal box-drawing in which each edge route has at most one bend and the total volume is O(Δ n^2), where n is the number of vertices and Δ is the maximum degree?

evidence.quote: Does every graph have a 1-bend drawing of volume O(∆n2)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A three-dimensional orthogonal box-drawing of a simple graph $G=(V,E)$ assigns to each vertex $v\in V$ an axis-aligned box (a rectangular parallelepiped with integer-coordinate corners) in $\mathbb{Z}^3$, with pairwise interior-disjoint boxes, and to each edge $uv\in E$ a polyline from a point on the surface of the box of $u$ to a point on the surface of the box of $v$, where each polyline segment is parallel to a coordinate axis, distinct edge polylines are interior-disjoint, and edge polylines avoid the interiors of all vertex boxes. A bend of an edge is an interior point of its polyline at which the segment changes direction. The drawing is called a 1-bend drawing if every edge polyline has at most one bend. The volume of the drawing is the number of unit grid cells in the smallest axis-aligned bounding box that contains the union of all vertex boxes and edge polylines.

Let $n=|V|$ and let $\Delta$ denote the maximum vertex degree of $G$.

Question: Does every simple graph $G$ admit a three-dimensional orthogonal box-drawing in which each edge has at most one bend and whose volume is $O(\Delta\, n^{2})$?
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work (notably Wood) established that every graph admits a 3-D orthogonal 1-bend box-drawing of volume $O(n^{3/2}m)$, which for an $m$-edge graph with maximum degree $\Delta$ gives roughly $O(\Delta\, n^{5/2})$. No reference was found establishing the stronger $O(\Delta n^{2})$ bound (or refuting it), so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Three-Dimensional Drawings (Handbook of Graph Drawing chapter)
status_evidence.snippet: Wood ... proved that every graph has a 3D orthogonal 1-bend box-drawing in O(n^{3/2} m) volume.
status_evidence.claim: Best known general 1-bend volume bound is O(n^{3/2} m), weaker than the conjectured O(Δ n^2).

status_evidence.title: 1-Bend 3-D Orthogonal Box-Drawings: Two Open Problems Solved (JGAA)
status_evidence.snippet: Does every graph have a 1-bend drawing of volume O(Δ n^2)?
status_evidence.claim: The question is posed as an open problem.
